body:
Thanks for this info!

Have you found the existing WPT tests comprehensive in this area? I was under the impression that this spec is somewhat lacking in test coverage.

Also, does your understanding of "context" align with what's on https://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/Contexts? (See also: #97.)

> Have you found the existing WPT tests comprehensive in this area? I was under the impression that this spec is somewhat lacking in test coverage.

The two relevant tests that I used were https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/document-metadata/the-link-element/link-style-error-quirks.html?product=servo and https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/document-metadata/the-link-element/link-style-error-limited-quirks.html?product=servo The latter is considered the base case, while the former has the exception. The latter is therefore confusingly named, but with it I was able to implement the logic as posted.

> Also, does your understanding of "context" align with what's on https://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/Contexts? (See also: https://github.com/whatwg/mimesniff/issues/97.)

Tbh, that's mostly a guess. The relevant part of the spec is https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-stylesheet:content-type-3 which calls https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/urls-and-fetching.html#content-type which is a minimal description. Based on the context of CSS, I assumed it would be style. Preferably this would be called out explicitly like I implemented in https://github.com/TimvdLippe/servo/blob/ee86dc6d916afcb78c2022a88204e27d4809854c/components/shared/net/lib.rs#L1108-L1127 where we pass the `load_context` from the caller (in this case [the `stylesheet_loader`](https://github.com/TimvdLippe/servo/blob/ee86dc6d916afcb78c2022a88204e27d4809854c/components/script/stylesheet_loader.rs#L366-L369) which therefore implies `style` context) to the `mime_classifier`
